title.narrative: UNICEF made significant contributions in improving diets, services, and practices in the Philippines. Achievements included the approval of the PhilHealth Benefit Package for Severe Acute Malnutrition and the inclusion of Multiple Micronutrient Supplements (MMS) in the Essential Medicines List. Through sustained advocacy, UNICEF supported the approval of the First 1,000 Days Social Protection cash grant for poor families under the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Programme (4Ps). UNICEF’s technical assistance trained 2,734 frontline workers, enhancing service delivery for 980,168;children;(503,709 boys and 476,459 girls);and 86,249 pregnant women. Globally, UNICEF advanced evidence-based solutions through impactful research on child wasting.;;
A nutrition policy or strategy to prevent undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in children under 5 years exists and is being implemented
